newsitem.title: CHINA: China bank issues Hong Kong currency credit card.
newsitem.headline: China bank issues Hong Kong currency credit card.

text.p: A Chinese provincial bank, the Guangdong Development Bank, will soon issue Visa International credit cards with billings made in Hong Kong dollars, the official Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
The news agency said the credit cards would be issued in some cities of the southern province of Guangdong.
Holders would be able to withdraw cash at VISA/Plus automated teller machines and make purchases abroad as well as in China.
China still maintains some restrictions on its currency, though it has been moving towards full convertibility.

Guangdong has been at the forefront of China's economic reforms. It has been highly successful in attracting foreign investment, much of it from Hong Kong, and the British colony's currency is widely used.
China has been trying to expand the use of credit cards to reduce the reliance on cash in the financial system.
Most of the cards issued have actually been debit cards, requiring the holder to deposit money in a bank account and then borrow against those funds.
Terms of the Guangdong Development Bank card were not immediately known.
Visa, a service association owned by 20,000 banks worldwide, has said it had 11 million cards on issue in China as of June last year.
